newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Congo wants OAU to withdraw Polisario recognition.
newsitem.headline: Congo wants OAU to withdraw Polisario recognition.

text.p: Congo's Prime Minister David Charles Ganao, whose country just cut its ties with the self- styled Saharan Arab Democratic Republic (SADR), on Wednesday urged African countries to reconsider their recognition.
Ganao, who is on a three-day official visit to Morocco, met King Hassan at the resort palace of Skhirat, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat on Tuesday, the Moroccan news agency MAP said.
Details of the meeting were not known but an official source said the talks were concentrated "on economic bilateral relations and mainly on the Western Sahara issue".

At a news conference, Ganao said "recognition of the RASD did not solve the Western Sahara dispute, in fact it led to serious divisions inside the Organisation of African Unity (OAU ...Time has come to say that its admission was a political mistake."
The Algeria-backed RASD was recognised by 70 countries, most of them members of the African organisation, including Congo.
Morocco walked out of the OAU in 1984 to protest against the SADR admission. The kingdom's seat in the Organisation has remained empty since.
Polisario, the military arm of the RASD, fought Morocco for nearly 17 years for the independence of the former Spanish colony before a U.N.-brokered ceasefire in September 1991.

A referendum of the Western Sahara's people, to decide on independence as sought by the Polisario, or integration with Morocco which controls four-fifth of the desert territory, was due in January 1992.
Despite U.N. efforts to draw up an electoral role, the vote has been delayed by wrangles over who, among the largely nomadic people, is eligible to take part.
Congo is the second African country this year to cut its ties with the SADR after Burkina Faso.
